label: Mark 12:1
text:
He began to speak to them in parables.
“A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and went into another country.

label: Mark 12:2
text: When it was time, he sent a servant to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

label: Mark 12:3
text: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.

label: Mark 12:4
text: Again, he sent another servant to them; and they threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.

label: Mark 12:5
text: Again he sent another; and they killed him; and many others, beating some, and killing some.

label: Mark 12:6
text: Therefore still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

label: Mark 12:7
text: But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

label: Mark 12:8
text: They took him, killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.

label: Mark 12:9
text: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.

label: Mark 12:10
text:
Haven’t you even read this Scripture:
‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the head of the corner.

label: Mark 12:11
text:
This was from the Lord,
it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

label: Mark 12:12
text: They tried to seize him, but they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spoke the parable against them. They left him, and went away.

label: Mark 12:13
text: They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, that they might trap him with words.

label: Mark 12:14
text: When they had come, they asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and don’t defer to anyone; for you aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?

label: Mark 12:15
text:
Shall we give, or shall we not give?”
But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them,
“Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”

label: Mark 12:16
text:
They brought it.
He said to them,
“Whose is this image and inscription?”
They said to him, “Caesar’s.”

label: Mark 12:17
text:
Jesus answered them,
“Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
They marveled greatly at him.

label: Mark 12:18
text: There came to him Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection. They asked him, saying,

label: Mark 12:19
text: “Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies, and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up offspring for his brother.’

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists τέκνον ('child') for אc2a B L W Δ Θ Ψ f1 579 700 892 and others, against τέκνα ('children') for P45 D f13 28 427 565 and others. The WEB prints 'children' (τέκνα). Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Washingtonianus are manuscript nodes of this graph; P45 is too.

label: Mark 12:20
text: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.

label: Mark 12:21
text: The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;

label: Mark 12:22
text: and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.

label: Mark 12:23
text: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”

label: Mark 12:24
text:
Jesus answered them,
“Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God?

label: Mark 12:25
text: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.

label: Mark 12:26
text: But about the dead, that they are raised; haven’t you read in the book of Moses, about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?

label: Mark 12:27
text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”

label: Mark 12:28
text: One of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together. Knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”

label: Mark 12:29
text:
Jesus answered,
“The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:

label: Mark 12:30
text:
you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’
This is the first commandment.

label: Mark 12:31
text:
The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
There is no other commandment greater than these.”

label: Mark 12:32
text: The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he,

label: Mark 12:33
text: and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

label: Mark 12:34
text:
When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him,
“You are not far from God’s Kingdom.”
No one dared ask him any question after that.

label: Mark 12:35
text:
Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple,
“How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?

label: Mark 12:36
text:
For David himself said in the Holy Spirit,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’

label: Mark 12:37
text:
Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?”

The common people heard him gladly.

label: Mark 12:38
text:
In his teaching he said to them,
“Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,

label: Mark 12:39
text: and the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts:

label: Mark 12:40
text: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”

label: Mark 12:41
text: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.

label: Mark 12:42
text: A poor widow came, and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.

label: Mark 12:43
text:
He called his disciples to himself, and said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,

label: Mark 12:44
text: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”

label: The Shema quoted in full
statement: Jesus opened his answer with the full Shema, 'Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one' (Deuteronomy 6:4), before the love command (Deuteronomy 6:5).

label: The scribe agrees; love exceeds sacrifices
statement: The scribe agreed that loving God with all one's heart, understanding, soul and strength, and one's neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices; Jesus told him he was not far from the kingdom of God, and no one dared ask him any question after that.

label: Scribes seek long robes, greetings and best seats
statement: In his teaching he warned against scribes who like to walk in long robes, receive greetings in the marketplaces, and take the best seats in the synagogues and the best places at feasts.

label: Scribes who devour widows' houses
statement: He accused scribes who devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers; they will receive greater condemnation.

label: The Temple treasury with collection chests
statement: He sat down opposite the treasury (gazophylakion) and saw the multitude casting money into it - the treasury was a place where worshipers deposited coin.

label: Two lepta, which make a quadrans
statement: A poor widow cast in two lepta, which together make a quadrans - the smallest coins in Judean circulation.

label: The widow gave all she had to live on
statement: The rich gave out of their abundance, but the widow out of her poverty gave all she had, her whole living.
